data.best_text: June to August for Suomenlinna and the outdoor terraces.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: Suomenlinna, Oodi and a sauna by the water.

stay.label: Long weekend
stay.text: Time for the Design District and a morning at the Market Square.

stay.label: Five days
stay.text: Add a day trip by ferry to Tallinn or by train to Porvoo.

areas.name: Kamppi and the centre
areas.text: Close to the railway station and the airport train. Everything within walking distance.

areas.name: Kallio
areas.text: Cheaper, younger and full of bars. Metro and tram into the centre.

areas.name: Punavuori
areas.text: Design shops and cafés, quiet in the evening.

transport.mode: Trains I and P from the airport
transport.text: About 27–32 minutes to the centre. You need an ABC ticket and can pay contactless.

events.name: Lux Helsinki
events.text: Light art on buildings and in parks. Free.

events.name: Vappu (Walpurgis Night and May Day)
events.text: Student caps, picnics in the parks and a carnival mood in the centre.

events.name: Flow Festival
events.text: Music festival in Suvilahti, on the old power plant site.

month_notes: Winter. The sea may be frozen.
The snow melts. Grey before things turn green.
Spring comes quickly and the outdoor terraces open.
Warmest, with the most life in the squares and the archipelago.
Dark and wet before the snow arrives.
The darkest time of the year. Christmas market on Senate Square.

prices.summary: Restaurants cost about the same as at home, but beer is more expensive.
tips: Eat lunch on weekdays. A lunch menu costs roughly 12–17 euros.

FI-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
FI-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not normally count as a travel document.
FI-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen, which also includes Iceland and Norway. Within the Nordics a Swedish driving licence can be enough in some cases, but a passport or national ID card is recommended.

FI-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
FI-fakta-mobil.summary: The same price as in Sweden for calls, texts and data.
FI-fakta-mobil.body: The EU's roaming rules apply: you pay as at home, but the operator may set a cap on data abroad.

FI-fakta-alkohol-18.title: Beer and wine from age 18
FI-fakta-alkohol-18.summary: Age 18 for drinks below 22 per cent.
FI-fakta-alkohol-18.body: Alko has a monopoly on drinks above 8 per cent. Weaker drinks are sold in ordinary shops.

FI-fakta-alkohol-20.title: Spirits from age 20
FI-fakta-alkohol-20.summary: Age 20 for drinks of 22 per cent or more.
FI-fakta-alkohol-20.body: The same age limits apply to anyone bringing alcohol into the country: nobody under 18, and only weak drinks before 20.

FI-helsingfors-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: Airport to the centre in half an hour
FI-helsingfors-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: Trains I and P run to the centre in about 27–32 minutes.
FI-helsingfors-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: The station is below the terminal. Both trains run to the central station in opposite directions around a ring line, so take whichever comes first. Buy an ABC ticket in the HSL app, from a machine or contactless.

FI-fakta-varldsarv.title: Aalto became World Heritage
FI-fakta-varldsarv.summary: Alvar Aalto's buildings are Finland's newest World Heritage Site.
FI-fakta-varldsarv.body: Five of the works are in Helsinki, among them Finlandia Hall.

FI-helsingfors-fakta-sveaborgsfarjan.title: The ferry to Suomenlinna runs on an ordinary ticket
FI-helsingfors-fakta-sveaborgsfarjan.summary: 15 minutes from the Market Square with an AB ticket.
FI-helsingfors-fakta-sveaborgsfarjan.body: The ferry runs all year from the east side of the Market Square, in front of the Presidential Palace. Buy a ticket before the gates: contactless, in the HSL app or from the machine on the quay. Cash is not accepted on board.

FI-helsingfors-sveaborg.name: Suomenlinna
FI-helsingfors-sveaborg.summary: A sea fortress on islands off the city, a World Heritage Site since 1991.
FI-helsingfors-sveaborg.body: Finland's first World Heritage Site together with Old Rauma.

FI-helsingfors-finlandiahuset.name: Finlandia Hall
FI-helsingfors-finlandiahuset.summary: Alvar Aalto's best-known building in the city, now World Heritage.
FI-helsingfors-finlandiahuset.body: One of five Aalto works in Helsinki on the World Heritage List.

FI-gamla-raumo.name: Old Rauma
FI-gamla-raumo.summary: A wooden town, a World Heritage Site since 1991.

FI-petajavesi.name: Petäjävesi Old Church
FI-petajavesi.summary: A wooden church, a World Heritage Site since 1994.

FI-sammallahdenmaki.name: Sammallahdenmäki
FI-sammallahdenmaki.summary: Bronze Age burial cairns, a World Heritage Site since 1999.

FI-kvarken.name: The Kvarken Archipelago
FI-kvarken.summary: Finland's only natural heritage site, since 2006.
FI-kvarken.body: Belongs together with the High Coast on the Swedish side.

FI-helsingfors-oodi.name: Helsinki Central Library Oodi
FI-helsingfors-oodi.summary: A three-storey library by the railway station. Free admission.
FI-helsingfors-oodi.body: Open Mon–Fri 8 am–9 pm and Sat–Sun 10 am–8 pm. Free wifi throughout the building.

bakverk-karelsk-pirog.name: Karelian pasty
bakverk-karelsk-pirog.hint: A rye crust with rice porridge, eaten with egg butter.

bakverk-korvapuusti.name: Korvapuusti
bakverk-korvapuusti.hint: A Finnish cinnamon bun, the name means a slap on the ear.

sevardhet-bastu-allman.name: Public sauna
sevardhet-bastu-allman.hint: A sauna anyone can go to, often by the water.

fardmedel-sparvagn-helsingfors.name: Tram in Helsinki
fardmedel-sparvagn-helsingfors.hint: Green and yellow, running through the whole inner city.

FI-helsingfors-ide-sveaborg.title: Half a day on Suomenlinna
FI-helsingfors-ide-sveaborg.body: Take the boat out to the fortress islands and walk around the ramparts.

FI-helsingfors-ide-aalto.title: Aalto walk
FI-helsingfors-ide-aalto.body: Start at Finlandia Hall and seek out more of Aalto's buildings.

FI-helsingfors-ide-oodi.title: Rainy day at Oodi
FI-helsingfors-ide-oodi.body: Go up to the top floor, read for a while and look out over the city.

FI-helsingfors-ide-helg.title: Helsinki over the weekend
FI-helsingfors-ide-helg.body: Suomenlinna for half a day, the Aalto walk and Oodi for the rest.

FI-present-muminmugg.name: Moomin mug
FI-present-muminmugg.body: Collectible mugs with new designs every year.

FI-present-choklad.name: Finnish milk chocolate
FI-present-choklad.body: The blue bar is in every shop.
